question: What does the word reality mean in the definition of the egg?
premises: If egg-nature applied too broadly, it would follow even in a principle made of qualities, subtle elements, and gross elements.
The answer turns on the meaning of the word reality.
That word refers to what consists of body, elements, and worlds.
inference: Therefore the word reality restricts egg-nature to the structured totality of body, elements, and worlds.
uncertainties: tanvakṣa is interpreted broadly as body and related constituents.
plain_english: If egg-nature were taken too broadly, it would apply even to a principle made only of qualities, subtle elements, and gross elements; but the word reality here means what consists of body, elements, and worlds.
